# Toolguard

> A Claude Code PreToolUse hook that replaces the native permission system for Bash, Read,
> Write, and Edit with regex/glob/native pattern matching, compound-command parsing, a
> hierarchical multi-level configuration model, an unoverridable hard-deny safety valve, and
> detailed logging.

Agents: read [docs/agent-guides.md](docs/agent-guides.md) first. It is the terse,
task-oriented version of the documentation (install, register hooks, write rules, diagnose
denials) and is usually sufficient on its own. Open the other guides only when a task needs
the detail -- they are verbose and human-oriented. For a heading-level index of every doc
below plus a question-and-pointer list for common lookups, see
[docs/agent-map.md](docs/agent-map.md).

## Agent docs (read first)

- [Guided install](docs/install.md): step-by-step runbook to install toolguard for a new user
  who pointed you at the repo -- scope/options (incl. takeover mode), `uv tool install`, hook
  registration, validation, optional migration/audit/maintenance, with every action journaled
  to ~/.toolguard/install-journal.md for a reversible rollback ([uninstall](docs/uninstall.md)).
- [Agent guides](docs/agent-guides.md): few-shot recipes for setting up and configuring
  toolguard on a user's behalf -- installation, registering hooks for every governed tool,
  governed_tools / additional_supported_tools, writing rules, and diagnosing denials.
- [Agent map](docs/agent-map.md): heading-level index of every doc, plus a
  question-and-pointer list of recurring questions ("where does `no_match_fallback` go",
  "what's the difference between `no_match_fallback` and `undecidable_fallback`", "is it OK
  to delete `~/.toolguard`", etc.) with one-line answers and links to the full detail.
- [Maintenance & audit skills](docs/skills.md): the toolguard-security-audit and
  toolguard-maintenance skills -- audit config for risk, and clean up / consolidate / promote
  rules with per-item consent.

## Core docs

- [Quick start](docs/quickstart.md): install, register hooks for all governed tools, declare
  governed_tools, add a few patterns, verify.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): full reference -- hook matchers, governed_tools,
  additional_supported_tools, environment variables, the hierarchy/resolution model,
  `additionalContext` rule enrichment, and the annotated config template.
- [Permission patterns](docs/permission-patterns.md): DEFAULT/REGEX/GLOB/NATIVE patterns, file-path
  patterns, path normalization, compound commands.
- [Takeover mode](docs/takeover-mode.md): blanket-allow + toolguard-enforces mode, its
  risks, and a complete example.
- [Auto-mode with toolguard](docs/auto-mode.md): running toolguard underneath Claude Code's
  own auto-accept / bypass-permissions modes -- what still gets enforced, the
  `allow_with_warning` fallback tradeoff, and how this differs from takeover mode.
- [Config sync & migration](docs/config-sync.md): divergence detection, migrating patterns,
  backups, and warning throttling.
- [Security best practices](docs/security.md): blanket-allow risks, recommended deny
  patterns, and verifying toolguard is actually running.

## Reference

- [README](README.md): project overview, requirements, installation, testing.
- [Architecture, as built](docs/architecture-as-built.md): design constraints, the external
  contract module, layer model, verdict altitudes, decision path, config hierarchy, pattern
  matching, the guarded config write path, logging streams.
- [Technical notes](technical-notes.md): deep design internals (hierarchy/resolution,
  hard-deny semantics, logging streams, subagent identification).

## Optional

- [Contributor guide (CLAUDE.md)](CLAUDE.md): conventions for agents modifying the toolguard
  repo itself -- not needed for configuring toolguard as a user.
